nodes.summary: If two dissimilarities on the same set satisfy `|d₁ x y - d₂ x y| ≤ η` for all `x, y`, then their single-linkage ultrametrics satisfy `|u₁ x y - u₂ x y| ≤ η` for all `x, y` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Lemma 15, stated there for two metrics on a finite set; the chain argument needs neither hypothesis).
nodes.title: Stability of single linkage in the sup norm

nodes.summary: The two-point metric space at distance `δ > 0` is sent to itself (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Thm. 18 (I)).
nodes.title: Condition (I)

nodes.summary: If `φ : X → Y` between finite metric spaces satisfies `d_X x x' ≥ d_Y (φ x) (φ x')`, then `u_X x x' ≥ u_Y (φ x) (φ x')` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Thm. 18 (II)).
nodes.title: Condition (II), functoriality

nodes.summary: Points are never merged below the separation of the space: if every nonzero distance is at least `s`, then `u x x' ≥ s` for `x ≠ x'` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Thm. 18 (III), `u(x, x') ≥ sep(X, d)`).
nodes.title: Condition (III)

nodes.summary: If every distance between distinct points is at least `s` and `r < s`, then `r`-equivalent points are equal (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Remark 19 on condition (III): the dendrogram is the partition into singletons for `t < sep(X, d)`).
nodes.title: Below the separation, clusters are singletons

nodes.summary: A hierarchical clustering method satisfying conditions (I), (II) and (III) is single linkage: `T X d = u*` for every finite metric space `(X, d)` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Thm. 18).
nodes.title: Characterization of single linkage (Carlsson–Mémoli)

nodes.summary: An assignment of a function `X → X → ℝ` to every dissimilarity on every finite type; `IsHCMethod` asks that metrics be sent to ultrametrics (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Def. 11).
nodes.title: Candidate hierarchical clustering methods

nodes.summary: `T` sends every finite metric space to an ultrametric on the same set (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Def. 11, with dendrograms identified with ultrametrics by their Thm. 9).
nodes.title: Hierarchical clustering method

nodes.summary: `d` is symmetric, zero exactly on the diagonal and satisfies the triangle inequality, so `(X, d)` is a metric space in the sense of Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), §2 (their finite metric spaces). It overlaps `CSLibExt`'s `MetricTSP.IsMetricCost`; `MathlibExt` cannot import `CSLibExt`, and Mathlib's metric classes are instance-based (one metric per type), which does not fit comparing several dissimilarities on…
nodes.title: Metric on a set, as a function

nodes.summary: On a finite metric space, `u*` is an ultrametric: symmetric, zero exactly on the diagonal and satisfying the strong triangle inequality (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Example 7: `T*` is a hierarchical clustering method).
nodes.title: Single linkage outputs an ultrametric

nodes.summary: A metric satisfying the strong triangle inequality `u x z ≤ max (u x y) (u y z)` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), §2). It duplicates `CSLibExt`'s `Bioinformatics.Phylogenetics.Splits.IsUltrametric` (same fields, the triangle inequality there following from the three-point condition), which `MathlibExt` cannot import; Mathlib's `IsUltrametricDist` is instance-based.
nodes.title: Ultrametric on a set, as a function

nodes.summary: If every distance between distinct points is at least `s`, then `u*(x, y) ≥ s` for `x ≠ y` (the fact that `T*` satisfies condition (III) of Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Thm. 18).
nodes.title: Single linkage never merges below the separation

nodes.summary: If `u` is symmetric, zero on the diagonal, satisfies the ultrametric inequality and `u ≤ d`, then `u ≤ u*` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Example 7, the remark after equation (4)). Together with `slDist_le` and `slDist_le_max`, `u*` is the largest ultrametric below `d` when `d ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Single linkage gives the maximal subdominant ultrametric

nodes.summary: `T*` is a hierarchical clustering method satisfying conditions (I), (II) and (III), so the hypotheses of Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Thm. 18 are consistent and single linkage is the method that theorem characterizes.
nodes.title: Single linkage satisfies the Carlsson–Mémoli axioms

nodes.summary: `u*(x, z) ≤ max (u*(x, y)) (u*(y, z))` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), §3.4, Example 7: `T*` is a hierarchical clustering method, so its output is an ultrametric).
nodes.title: The single-linkage distance is an ultrametric

nodes.summary: `u*(x, y) ≤ d(x, y)` whenever `d(x, y) ≥ 0` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Example 7, the remark after equation (4)).
nodes.title: The single-linkage ultrametric is below the dissimilarity

nodes.summary: For a dissimilarity `d`, `slDist d x y` is the infimum of the scales `r ≥ 0` at which `x` and `y` are `r`-equivalent, i.e. the infimum over chains `x = x₀, …, x_k = y` of the largest hop. On a finite set the infimum is attained and this is the ultrametric `u*` of Carlsson and Mémoli (JMLR 11 (2010), Example 7, equation (4)), the maximal sub-dominant ultrametric, which encodes the single-linkage dendrogram (Lemma 12…
nodes.title: Single-linkage ultrametric

nodes.summary: In a (pseudo)metric space, two points are `r`-equivalent exactly when they are joined by a path in the `r`-neighbourhood graph, the one-skeleton of `VR(M, r)`. So the single-linkage clusters at scale `r` are `π₀` of the Vietoris–Rips complex (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, §3.2).
nodes.title: Single-linkage clusters are the connected components of the Rips graph

nodes.summary: On a finite set and for `r ≥ 0`, `x` and `y` are `r`-equivalent if and only if `u*(x, y) ≤ r` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Lemma 12 and Remark 13). Finiteness makes the infimum defining `u*` a minimum.
nodes.title: The dendrogram is the family of closed balls of `u*`

nodes.summary: A distance non-increasing map `f : (X, d) → (Y, e)` (that is, `e (f x) (f y) ≤ d x y`) sends `r`-equivalent points to `r`-equivalent points, hence maps each cluster of `X` into a cluster of `Y` at every scale. This is Carlsson's functoriality of clustering (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, Def. 3.2, there for distance-preserving maps) and the property behind condition (II) of the characterization of…
nodes.title: Functoriality of single-linkage clustering

nodes.summary: If `r ≤ s`, `r`-equivalent points are `s`-equivalent, so the clusters at scale `r` refine those at scale `s` and together form a dendrogram (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Example 2).
nodes.title: Single-linkage clusters are nested

nodes.summary: If `d₂ ≤ d₁ + η` pointwise, then `r`-equivalence for `d₁` implies `(r + η)`-equivalence for `d₂`: the chain argument in the proof of Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Lemma 15.
nodes.title: Perturbing the dissimilarity shifts the scale

nodes.summary: An `r`-chain from `x` to `y` followed by an `s`-chain from `y` to `z` is a `max r s`-chain from `x` to `z`; this is the ultrametric inequality for `u*` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Example 1 and Example 7).
nodes.title: Chains concatenate

nodes.summary: For a dissimilarity `d : X → X → ℝ` and a scale `r`, `SLEquiv d r` is the equivalence relation generated by `d x y ≤ r`: `x` and `y` are `r`-equivalent when they are joined by a finite chain `x = x₀, x₁, …, x_k = y` whose consecutive points satisfy `d xᵢ xᵢ₊₁ ≤ r` (up to the order of the arguments of `d`). Its classes are the single-linkage clusters at scale `r` (Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Example 1;…
nodes.title: `r`-equivalence (single-linkage clusters at scale `r`)

nodes.summary: The space `{p, q}` with `d(p, q) = δ`, here on `Bool`; the space `({p, q}, (0 δ; δ 0))` of Carlsson and Mémoli, JMLR 11 (2010), Thm. 18 (I).
nodes.title: The two-point metric space

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
